title: Choose the Product Passport composition
question: All three keep the trusted Product Passport content and the dark, depth-led reference language. Which composition should become the production direction?

options.label: Vault Transfer
options.thesis: The product and its primary measurement read as two sides of one transparent transfer surface.
options.viewport: A complete left product bay faces one large right-side glass chamber linking 240 mg to its 709 ml serving; actions float above and the four-column evidence ledger anchors the bottom.
options.risk: The transfer metaphor must remain descriptive and never imply a recommendation or conversion.

options.label: Cinematic Shelf
options.lineage: A wide optical readout with an open data field
options.thesis: The product image is the physical anchor while one oversized number occupies a quiet, borderless field of depth.
options.viewport: The complete left image bay runs the full hero height; the right side is mostly open space with the product name, a monumental 240 mg readout, a slim metric shelf, and the evidence columns below.
options.risk: The open composition needs disciplined contrast so quiet metadata does not disappear into atmosphere.

options.label: Lens Stack
options.lineage: Overlapping focus planes from an optical instrument
options.thesis: Three shallow glass planes let caffeine, serving context, and sugar resolve one layer at a time without hiding their labels.
options.viewport: A complete product bay holds the left half while three offset measurement panes stack on the right; the active front pane carries 240 mg, and a single four-column information band remains fully legible below.
options.risk: Layering must create hierarchy, not make factual states appear unavailable or blurred.
